Our Club

Our club is dedicated to bringing Judo to the widest audience under our founder, head coach and former Olympian Alonzo Henderson 6th Dan OLY → since 2011.
Judo is a martial art and Olympic sport practiced in 200+ countries round the world and is based on the 8 core values of friendship, honor, respect, modesty, politeness, courage, self-control, and sincerity.

🥋 Official Syllabus • Examination & Study Hub

Mastering the Belt Pathway: The Cabra Judo Grading System & Digital Study Hub

David Moloney (Assistant Coach & Secretary) 📅 September 18, 2026 • 4 min read

At Cabra Judo Club, earning your next belt is a testament to consistent practice, technical mastery, and dojo spirit. Fully aligned with the Irish Judo Association (IJA) syllabus and International Judo Federation (IJF) standards, our structured grading pathway guides every judoka from their very first white belt through junior Mon ranks, senior Kyu grades, and national Dan promotion.

🔴 Junior Mon System (Under 14s)

Structured progression across 1st to 18th Mon (Red, Yellow, Orange, Green, Blue, Brown). Emphasizes safe breakfalls (Ukemi), fundamental throws (Gokyo), hold-downs (Osaekomi-waza), Kodomo no Kata, and Japanese terminology.

Explore Mon Study Guide →

🟢 Senior Kyu System (14+ & Adults)

From 6th Kyu (White/Red) to 1st Kyu (Brown Belt). Candidates master advanced throwing mechanics (Nage-waza), combinations (Renraku-waza), counters (Kaeshi-waza), armlocks (Kansetsu-waza), and strangles (Shime-waza).

Explore Kyu Study Guide →

⚫ Dan Grade Pathway (Black Belts)

The journey to 1st Dan (Shodan) and beyond under the mentorship of 1980 Olympian Sensei Alonzo Henderson 6th Dan OLY. Requires formal Kata proficiency (Nage-no-Kata, Katame-no-Kata), competition points, and service to judo.

Read Sensei Alonzo's Profile →

📋 Interactive Grading Portal

Our bespoke online grading software enables coaches to record candidate evaluations, track syllabus requirements, generate official printable certificates, and manage testing records directly on the tatami.

Launch Grading Portal →
🥋

The Three Pillars of Grading: Shin, Gi & Tai (心・技・体)

In traditional Japanese martial arts, a belt promotion is not simply about learning moves; it represents the harmonious growth of three core dimensions:

• Shin (心 - Mind & Spirit): Dojo etiquette (Reiho), respect, humility, regular attendance, and emotional composure under pressure (Fudoshin).
• Gi (技 - Skill & Technique): Flawless off-balancing (Kuzushi), entry positioning (Tsukuri), decisive completion (Kake), and deep understanding of Japanese terminology.
• Tai (体 - Body & Conditioning): Safe, dynamic breakfalls (Ukemi), core fitness, balance, and the stamina to apply techniques effectively during free sparring (Randori).

Grading examinations are held periodically at Lindsay Road National School throughout the academic season. Candidates are invited by coaches once attendance and technical prerequisites are fulfilled.
